Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this — we're finalizing the order form and we need to confirm a few items in the assurance/addendum section before procurement will sign. High level asks from our security team below: 

- Tenancy isolation: can you confirm whether Helix will be logically separated from other tenants for audit access (we don't require dedicated hardware, but need assurances about scoped access and environment tagging).
- Pen test window: we typically provide a 2-week window and 30 days notice; curious what works operationally for Redwood and whether there are staging constraints.
- Evidence cadence: SOC 2 report cadence (annual) is fine, but we also need a list of reproducible evidence (sample logs, retention windows, contact for pen test coordination).

I attached our SOC2 questionnaire to give you a sense of the artifacts the team will request. Can you share a proposed assurance wording we can circulate with procurement/legal?

Thanks — happy to set a quick sync if easier.

Maya — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary and proposal below; happy to update language after legal reviews.

Tenancy isolation
- Redwood is multi-tenant by default but we can commit to logical tenancy controls in the order form: environment tagging, access-scoped roles, and explicit acceptance that scans/inspections will be limited to Helix-tagged resources. We cannot promise physical separation without dedicated capacity (we can call that out as an option).

Pen test timing
- Operationally we propose a standard 14-day window with 30 days notice. For tooling/ops reasons, pen tests must run against a staging or pre-prod environment that mirrors production and is tenant-tagged; production-only attacks require a separate exception and a stricter coordination plan.

Evidence cadence
- SOC 2 Type II (annual) plus: sample logs (90-day retention extracts), configuration snapshots (30-day retention for infra configs), and a named security contact for coordination. We can provide a standard evidence checklist that maps to the questionnaire you shared.

Proposed next steps
1) I'll loop in Legal with suggested wording (Assurance Addendum + limited audit rights scope).
2) We can attach a short operational annex that lists pen-test rules of engagement and evidence artifacts.
3) If that looks OK, send over procurement timeline and we'll route a DocuSign envelope for the order form + addendum.

Attached: OrderForm_HelixHealth_v3.pdf (pdf) — current draft.

If helpful I can set a 30-min call this week to walk Legal through the proposed annex.

Best,

Forwarding my quick redline summary for Vanessa to share with Helix. I kept changes narrow to preserve our operational commitments while addressing typical customer asks. Quoted below is the proposed language; I'll attach a Word redline.

Redline highlights (summary)
- Audit rights: limited to documentation review and remote evidence requests in production; for on-site or live-traffic deep inspections we require tenant-tagged environment or Dedicated capacity. Limit audit frequency to annual by default; additional inspections allowed by mutual agreement and with 30 days' notice.
- Pen testing: allow Helix (and their designated testers) to perform penetration testing subject to: (a) 30 days' prior written notice; (b) tests run in a pre-prod/staging environment by default; (c) agreed rules of engagement and safety kill-switch; (d) no simulated social engineering without explicit approval.
- Data access & scoping: auditors must be scoped to Helix data and access must be read-only for evidence pulls; production data extracts require narrow agreed queries and must be logged.
- Evidence cadence & artifacts: we propose mapping Helix's questionnaire to a 30-item evidence checklist (SOC2 report, system configs, sampling of logs, recent change records). Turnaround target for standard evidence request: 10 business days; for deeper forensic requests we will confirm timelines per request.

I attached an editable addendum called assurance_addendum_redline.docx with the specific clause text — we should share that with Helix and let procurement/legal mark up.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
